ACTION: Read `~/.claude/skills/subagent-driven-development/references/fix-loop.md`. The skill requires this before every fix round, and it sets the re-review rules.
ACTION: Read `fetch/retry.py` around line 41. I check whether `attempt` starts at 0 or 1 and whether the first call counts. This confirms that `>=` is the correct change before I make it.
ACTION: Read `tests/test_retry.py` to see how it fakes the timeout.
ACTION: Edit `tests/test_retry.py`. Add a test where the fetch always times out. It asserts the fetch runs exactly the configured number of times. Run it and confirm it fails on the current code.
ACTION: Edit `fetch/retry.py:41`. Change `attempt > max_retries` to `attempt >= max_retries`.
ACTION: Run `tests/test_retry.py`, then the full suite. Confirm the new test passes and nothing else breaks.
ACTION: Commit the test and the fix together on the task branch.
ACTION: Run `scripts/review-package` on `specs/plans/14-buoy-sync.md` with BASE as the commit the reviewer saw and HEAD as the new commit. Keep the diff path it reports.
ACTION: Dispatch a scoped re-review with `re-review-prompt.md` on model `sonnet`. The prompt holds F1 verbatim and the diff path. It asks for ADDRESSED or NOT ADDRESSED on F1 and for any new Critical or Important issue.
ACTION: If the re-review is clean, append `Task 4: complete (commits <base7>..<head7>, review clean)` to `.sdd/14-buoy-sync/progress.md`. Then start Task 5.

Fixing F1 (the off-by-one retry finding) myself, as you asked. I send no fix subagent. I still send one scoped re-review, because a fix I wrote should not close its own Important finding. Tell me if you want that skipped.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The old test checked only that a retry happens. An off-by-one in a retry limit passes that kind of test, so the new test counts the calls.
- I write the test first and watch it fail. That proves it can catch this bug, and the one-character change then turns it green.
